newsitem.title: USA: Aetrium sees Q4 results below estimates.
newsitem.headline: Aetrium sees Q4 results below estimates.

text.p: Aetrium Inc, which supplies technologies and equipment used by the semiconductor industry, on Thursday said it expected fourth-quarter revenue and profit to be below analysts' expectations.
Aetrium said it expected fourth-quarter revenue of about $11 million, and earnings per share of about $0.15 versus the mean estimate of $0.21.
The company plans to report its fourth-quarter results on February 5.
Analysts had estimated revenues of about $13 million.
In the 1995 fourth quarter, the company reported earnings of $0.37 a share on revenues of $15.1 million.
"For the first three quarters of the year, bookings were below our billings, consistent with the industry-wide slow down," said Joseph Levesque, president and chief executive.

"During the third quarter, we announced that we would manage our backlog to bring bookings and billings closer to parity. Orders were weaker than we had hoped in the first part of the current quarter, although they have improved substantially since mid-November," he said in a statement.
However, the strength in orders late in the quarter was not enough to maintain its existing backlog, so the company said it decided to slow shipments to about $11 million.

Levesque said Aetrium is working closely with its customers to reschedule some shipments while keeping within their plans, and believes there is no risk that any orders may be canceled as a result of slowing shipments.

"We have growing confidence that we saw the bottom in the current cycle early in the fourth quarter," Levesque said. "Our orders will be significantly higher in the fourth quarter than they were in the third quarter," he said.

"Given the recent strength that we have seen in orders, and given the positive turn that such industry indicators as the book-to-bill ratios for semiconductors and semiconductor capital equipment have taken, we are anticipating sequentially higher revenue throughout 1997," he added.
